hero: An adult hemodialysis unit in a provincial Philippine town, mid-morning. A thirteen-year-old Filipino boy reclines in a dialysis chair, pale, one hand on his forehead. A nurse lowers the chair while a young male physician on duty kneels to check the boy, a phone to his ear as he speaks with the specialist; the boy's mother stands close with a towel. Dialysis machines and adult patients in the background, soft natural light, calm urgency, no text.

figures.teaches: Why fluid removal and urea removal strike a child harder: small volume reserve and the urea gradient into the brain.
figures.content: Left panel title 'Volume'. A bucket labeled 'Adult' and a cup labeled 'Child', each losing an identical glass labeled 'Same removal'. Below the cup: heart icon with arrow up labeled 'Pulse rises first', then BP icon with arrow down labeled 'Pressure falls late'. Right panel title 'Osmoles'. Blood vessel beside a brain; urea dots leave blood fast (arrow labeled 'Urea falls fast'), fewer leave brain (label 'Brain urea lags'); blue water arrows into brain labeled 'Water moves in'. Symptoms list under brain: 'Headache', 'Vomiting', 'Confusion', 'Seizure'.

figures.teaches: For each chair emergency, the early sign in a child, the first action, and whether blood is returned.
figures.content: Table with three columns 'Early sign', 'First action', 'Return blood?'. Rows: 'Hypotension' (Pulse rising, yawning / Lay flat, stop removal / Yes); 'Disequilibrium' (Headache, vomiting / Slow or stop, call / Yes); 'Air' (Foam, breathless / Clamp, stop pump / No); 'Hemolysis' (Cherry-red blood / Stop, keep circuit / No); 'Dialyzer reaction' (Itch, wheeze / Stop pump / No if severe); 'Needle out' (Blood on sheet / Clamp, pressure / No); 'Seizure' (Fitting / Protect, glucose, call / If stopped). Banner: 'Stop the pump for air, hemolysis, reaction, blood loss'.

figures.teaches: The path of dialysis water and what DOH AO 2013-0003 requires at each sampling point.
figures.content: Left to right pipe: 'Raw water' (sample point 1) -> 'Pretreatment' -> 'Carbon' (label 'Removes chloramine') -> 'Reverse osmosis' -> 'Product water' (sample point 2) -> 'Loop' -> 'Machine' (sample point 3 'Point of use') -> child icon. Under pipe: 'Microbiology: all 3 points, monthly'; 'Chemistry: point of use, every 6 months'; 'TDS: weekly logbook'. Badge: 'Medical director responsible'. No contaminant limit numbers.

card: A dialysis machine beside a small chair with a child's school backpack and a water-treatment pipe in soft focus behind, warm light, no text.
